# Aomi

> Agentic AI infrastructure for blockchain. Embed a chat widget that simulates and signs transactions through the user's own wallet, build custom UIs on the headless React library, or add your product's API as a callable AI tool. Non-custodial by design — Aomi never holds keys.

The fastest entry point for an agent is `/agents.md` — it routes the user's intent to the right install path. The full corpus is `/llms-full.txt` (every doc plus both skill files concatenated, for one-fetch ingestion).

Safety mantra: Read by default. Simulate before sign. Credentials never round-trip.

## Start here

- [Agent onboarding](https://aomi.dev/agents.md): Routes user intent to one of three paths — transact via CLI, embed UI, or add a new tool. Read this first.
- [Build an Aomi app](https://aomi.dev/agents/build): HTML agent landing page for app-building prompts.
- [Transact with Aomi](https://aomi.dev/agents/transact): HTML agent landing page for transaction prompts.
- [Build markdown mirror](https://aomi.dev/agents/build.md): Raw markdown mirror of the build guide.
- [Transact markdown mirror](https://aomi.dev/agents/transact.md): Raw markdown mirror of the transact guide.
- [Full corpus](https://aomi.dev/llms-full.txt): All docs and skills concatenated. Use when you need everything in one fetch.

## For agents acting on a wallet

Use these when the user wants to read prices/balances or build/sign transactions.

- [aomi-transact skill](https://github.com/aomi-labs/skills/blob/main/aomi-transact/SKILL.md): The canonical operating procedure for driving the `aomi` CLI — chat, simulate, sign. Includes hard rules on credentials and signing.
- [CLI reference](https://aomi.dev/docs/reference/cli.md): Full command list with flags. Read after the skill if you need a flag the skill didn't show.
- [Account abstraction](https://aomi.dev/docs/reference/account-abstraction.md): AA-first signing, mode fallback (7702 vs 4337), provider selection, sponsorship, per-chain RPC guidance.
- [Simulation](https://aomi.dev/docs/reference/simulation.md): How forked-chain simulation works and when to require it.

## For agents embedding Aomi UI

Use these when the user wants to add an Aomi chat widget to their own app.

- [Quickstart](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/quickstart.md): Install the widget into a Next.js app via one shadcn command. Start here.
- [Integration guide](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/integration-guide.md): Decide between the bundled widget and the headless React library.
- [Headless: install](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/headless/install.md): Install `@aomi-labs/react` and wire up the runtime.
- [Headless: runtime provider](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/headless/runtime-provider.md): The provider that holds backend connection, session, and tool state.
- [Headless: hooks](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/headless/hooks.md): React hooks for chat, tools, sessions, control state.
- [Headless: build custom UI](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/headless/build-custom-ui.md): Patterns for composers, message lists, tool views.
- [Widget: AomiFrame](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/widget/aomi-frame.md): The bundled chat component and its props.
- [Widget: components](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/widget/components.md): The composable widget pieces (header, composer, control bar).
- [Widget: configuration](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/widget/configuration.md): App, model, theme, control surface options.
- [Widget: theming](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/ui/widget/theming.md): Color tokens, fonts, spacing.
- [Wallet integration](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/services/wallet-integration.md): Para and wagmi setup; how the widget gets a signer.

## For agents extending Aomi with new tools

Use these when the user wants to add their product or API as something Aomi can call.

- [aomi-build skill](https://github.com/aomi-labs/skills/blob/main/aomi-build/SKILL.md): The canonical procedure for converting an OpenAPI/SDK/repo into an Aomi SDK app crate. Includes tool design rules and validation steps.
- [Building apps](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/services/building-apps.md): Aomi App architecture — what an app is, how it's invoked, what it returns.
- [Namespaces](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/namespaces.md): Tool naming conventions and when to use which.
- [API reference](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/services/api-reference.md): The HTTP API the backend exposes.
- [Sessions (backend)](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/services/sessions.md): How conversation state, tool calls, and tx state persist across turns.
- [SDK reference](https://aomi.dev/docs/reference/sdk.md): The React SDK surface — components, hooks, types.

## Concepts and architecture

Read for context, not as the entry point.

- [Overview](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/overview.md): What Aomi is and how the parts fit together.
- [How it works](https://aomi.dev/docs/build/how-it-works.md): The simulation-first transaction pipeline, end-to-end.
- [Architecture](https://aomi.dev/docs/reference/architecture.md): System diagram and component boundaries.
- [Runtime](https://aomi.dev/docs/reference/runtime.md): The hosted backend that runs Aomi Apps.

## Channels (humans, not agents)

Background context for understanding how end-users actually reach Aomi.

- [Telegram bot](https://aomi.dev/docs/use-aomi/telegram/overview.md): Aomi as a Telegram trading bot.
- [Web chat](https://aomi.dev/docs/use-aomi/web/overview.md): The hosted aomi.dev playground.
- [FAQ](https://aomi.dev/docs/use-aomi/faq.md): Common end-user questions.
